info.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash Video Extend
info.description: Extend one input video using optional reference images and a text prompt

post.description:
- Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash (`gemini-omni-1.2-flash-video-extend`) continues an input video with native audio, optionally guided by reference images.
- **Video:** `video_urls` requires exactly 1 video, up to 30 seconds.
- **Images:** Optionally supply up to 10 reference images via `image_urls`.
- **Duration:** `duration` is the number of seconds to append, default `3`; it is not the total output duration.
- **Aspect ratio:** `aspect_ratio` accepts only `auto` and defaults to `auto`; output ratio follows the input.
- **Billing:** The output video portion is charged for the appended seconds. The full input video duration, reference images, prompt, and model reasoning also contribute to usage; settlement is based on actual usage.
- **Resolution:** `quality` accepts `360p`, `720p`, `1080p`, `4k`, or `auto`; default `auto` follows the input. Explicit values can raise or lower output resolution.
- Synchronized native audio is generated automatically, with no additional parameter.
- Write negative requirements directly in `prompt`; there is no separate negative prompt parameter.
- Set `seed` to improve reproducibility.
- Asynchronous processing: [query task status](/en/api-manual/task-management/get-task-detail) using the returned task ID.
- Generated video links remain valid for 24 hours; save them promptly.

prompt.description:
Text prompt describing what should happen after the input video ends.

Supports Chinese and English. For more stable results, describe the desired action and changes clearly. Write negative requirements directly in `prompt`, such as `No dialogue` or `No text`; there is no separate negative prompt parameter.

The prompt is required and must not be empty or contain only whitespace.
prompt.example: The person continues walking forward and slowly exits the frame.

video_urls.description: Exactly one directly reachable HTTP/HTTPS MP4, no longer than 30 seconds.

image_urls.description:
Optional reference image array, up to 10 images. It may be used with the video being extended to constrain subjects, style, or elements.

**Input requirements:**
- HTTP/HTTPS image URLs only
- Supported formats: `png`, `jpeg`, `webp`

**Billing:** Every reference image contributes input tokens.

duration.description:
Appended video duration in seconds; default `3`.

**Notes:**
- Accepts any integer from `3` to `10`
- Specifies how many seconds are generated after the input video, not the total output duration
- Total output duration = input video duration + `duration`
- Appended duration directly affects billing

quality.description:
Output video resolution; default `auto`.

- `360p`: short edge 360.
- `720p`: short edge 720.
- `1080p`: short edge 1080.
- `4k`: short edge 2160.
- `auto`: follows the input resolution; this is the default.

Choosing an explicit value can raise or lower output resolution.

**Billing:** Output video tokens increase with output resolution. Input video also contributes tokens; higher resolution costs more.

aspect_ratio.description: Only auto is accepted and it is the default. Output aspect ratio follows the input video.

seed.description:
Random seed; random by default.

- Range: `0`–`4294967295`.
- Fixing the seed reduces variation from parameter changes when tuning prompts and improves reproducibility.

callback_url.description:
HTTPS callback URL to notify when the task completes

**Callback timing:**
- Triggered when the task completes (completed), fails (failed), or is cancelled (cancelled)
- Sent after billing is confirmed

**Security restrictions:**
- HTTPS protocol only
- Callbacks to internal IP addresses are forbidden (127.0.0.1, 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x, etc.)
- URL length must not exceed `2048` characters

**Callback mechanism:**
- Timeout: `10` seconds
- Up to `3` retries on failure (retried `1`s / `2`s / `4`s after each failure respectively)
- The callback body format matches the response of the task query endpoint
- A 2xx status code from the callback URL is treated as success; other status codes trigger a retry
